anomalies.observed: On the single sheet, a wire runs from J1 pin 14 (PIN14) diagonally up to the global label 'M-BUS' and continues into J6 pin 4, which carries the PORTB2 label. J2 pin 14 has no such wire, so J1 and J2 are not identical pass-through connectors, and the unrelated bus pin 14 is merged onto the PortB unit signal line.
anomalies.expected: Spec: J1/J2 are 'identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through)', and J6 is 'M5Unit PortB breakout (GND, +5V, two GPIOs), passed through from J1/J2' — i.e. J6 pin 4 should sit on the PORTB2 net (J1/J2 pin 3) only, and J1 pin 14 should pass through to J2 pin 14 unaltered.

evidence.quote: diagonal wire from J1 PIN14 (pin 14) to global label 'M-BUS' terminating at J6 pin 4 (PORTB2); J2 pin 14 has no corresponding wire (sheet m5-pantilt, columns 3-4)
J6 | Conn_01x04 | M5Unit PortB breakout (GND, +5V, two GPIOs), passed through from J1/J2.
Top and bottom M5Stack bus connectors; identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through).

anomalies.impact: The PortB unit connector's signal pin is shorted to M5Stack bus pin 14 (an unrelated GPIO), and the J1→J2 pass-through for pin 14 is broken; plugging an M5Unit PortB device would load/conflict with GPIO14 and the stacked module above would not see the expected net.
